## Background

Split from umbrella bug 53f9-a218-8799-49be (closed as superseded). 53f9 covered four flaky-test sub-tracks; Track A (test-merge-to-main*.sh) was closed by PR #221, but three other sub-tracks remained. This ticket covers Track B.

## Symptom

`tests/scripts/test-write-cycle-ledger.sh` fails intermittently in CI. Same commit, same code — pass on one run, fail on the next.

## Investigation findings (BASIC tier, recorded on 53f9 during P2 triage)

The original /tmp race hypothesis was disproved: the test uses `mktemp -d` isolation throughout, so cross-test /tmp pollution is not the cause.

The most likely remaining culprit is the concurrent-write test (around line 130) which launches 3 parallel writes and then asserts on the resulting state. The assertion window is non-atomic — the test reads the state file between the parallel writes' independent fsync points, so the observed state can be partial under load.

## Affected files

* tests/scripts/test-write-cycle-ledger.sh (concurrent-write subtest near line 130)
* Possibly: plugins/dso/scripts/write-cycle-ledger.sh state-file lifecycle

## Proposed approach

1. Add a barrier (`wait` for all 3 parallel writers to complete) before the assertion, so the read happens after all writes synced.
2. Or, if the parallel-write contract is itself the test's behavior under test, assert on a property that holds in any interleaving (e.g., 'at least one entry was written and all entries have valid schema') rather than an exact count or order.

## References

* Umbrella ticket: 53f9-a218-8799-49be (closed as superseded)
* Detected_by: tests
